what_this_is: Citations that existed before `citable means verified` was enforced and whose quote could not be confirmed on the retrievable page. Enumerated so the rule can block NEW defects without the repo going red on old ones. This is debt, not permission: a citation is only in here because a human-run pass put it here, and nothing adds to it automatically.
rule: tools/validate_card_profiles.py errors on any unverified citation NOT listed here. Removing an entry (by re-sourcing or downgrading the claim) is the only way to burn it down.

entries.why: publisher refuses automated retrieval (HTTP 200); page content never seen
entries.owner_decision_basis: tools/stamp_verification.py states the disposition already: "`unreachable` is not a failure verdict. A page that cannot be retrieved proves nothing about the record; conflating 'I could not check it' with 'it is wrong' would be the same overreach this repo keeps catching elsewhere. Those records stay citable, carry their reason, and are counted in every report so they never become invisible." The decision is the owner's written policy, recorded here rather than re-asked.

entries.why: PAGE DRIFT, not a bad citation: the identical quote hash stamped `exact` on 2026-09-10 and `partial` on 2026-09-11 from the same fetch path. The repo did not change; the page did, or the fetch is unstable. A `partial` verdict is a needs-a-reader bucket by design, so this is R2 work (a person decides), not re-sourcing. Added deliberately with its measurement rather than left to block every phase.

research_note: Every entry probed 2026-09-11 through tools/verify_snippets' fetcher -- the same path the gate uses, deliberately not tools/capture.py, because two fetch paths that disagree is what produced 13 of 39 drifts in the repair batch. `research.gate_path_verdict` is what the gate can actually see.

classes.record excerpt too narrow: quote is on the page, outside the record's stored snippet -- re-capture the record
classes.quote not on the page: quote is genuinely absent through the gate's path -- re-source or downgrade to proposed
classes.page cannot be retrieved: decided by written policy: stays citable, carries its reason
